rules.statement: In production code, don't build a URL or origin the server publishes to a client (an issuer, an API base, a discovery or bootstrap value) from the request's scheme, `Host` header or `HttpRequest` origin; take it from the stored, validated or configured value.
rules.why: A forged or proxied `Host`, or a shared cache that stores one host's response under another, would send the user to sign in at an authority nobody configured, or send the access token to another origin.
rules.check: Look for published URL fields assembled from `Request.Scheme`, `Request.Host`, `GetDisplayUrl`, `UriHelper.BuildAbsolute` or similar request-derived origins.

rules.statement: In production code, when no configured or stored issuer exists for a document that must publish one, fail with a problem response that names the setting to configure; don't fall back to the request origin.
rules.why: A missing issuer is a configuration error, and a request-origin fallback is an unvalidated second source of the same value.
rules.check: Look for null-coalescing or fallback branches that use the request's scheme and host when the configured issuer or tenant issuer is missing.

rules.statement: In production code, publish a same-origin API base to a browser as a root-relative path built from the host's path base (for example `/` or `/identity`), and use an absolute URL only when an explicit setting overrides it.
rules.why: The browser resolves a root-relative value against the origin that served the bundle, so the `Host` header contributes nothing and a path-base deployment works without configuration.
rules.check: Look for an API base URL default built as an absolute URL from the request, or one that ignores `PathBase`.

rules.statement: In production code, a frontend's configured issuer must be exactly the serving tenant's stored issuer, the same value its OpenID discovery document publishes, or an explicit override; don't derive or normalize it separately.
rules.why: The issuer a bundle trusts has to equal the issuer its tokens carry, under every tenant-resolution strategy.
rules.check: Look for client bootstrap or config code that computes the issuer itself (string building, trailing-slash changes) instead of reading the tenant's stored issuer or the configured override.

rules.statement: In production code, send `Cache-Control: no-store` on a response whose content depends on the serving tenant or host.
rules.why: A shared cache could otherwise serve one tenant's or host's values for another.
rules.check: Look for tenant- or host-dependent endpoints, such as bootstrap or config documents, that set no cache headers or set public caching.
